answer: Each agent may submit work, but payment is released only after a randomly assigned peer verifies the result and stakes its own earned credits on that judgment. A fraudster can mint a thousand identities, yet those accounts cannot cheaply manufacture independent, accountable reviewers: colluding reviewers risk forfeiting credits, and repeated agreement patterns expose the ring. The basalt ledger records stakes and outcomes; a harbor of honest reviewers keeps review accessible, while a crystal-clear penalty makes each fake identity costly to sustain.
